title: Sabha electricity workers' union protest over unpaid salary arrears
scope: City-level union-organized protest reported in Sabha
participants_original: An unspecified number of Sabha electricity workers participated in a union-organized protest; reports say workers across departments and maintenance teams stopped work but give no protest attendance.
threshold_50_evidence: A physical protest is reported, but neither article gives a concurrent crowd count; workforce scope and work stoppage do not establish 50 attendees.

start_date.summary: Alwasat’s Jan24 report dates the union-organized protest to Sunday Jan24.

location.summary: The report places the protest in Sabha; venue is not specified.

organizer.summary: The event was organized by the Libyan Electricity Workers Union.

demands.summary: Workers demanded unpaid 2017–2020 salary arrears from the General Electricity Company of Libya.

participants_original.summary: Reports identify electricity workers and maintenance teams but provide no protest headcount.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A protest is described, but no concurrent count or explicit size estimate is reported.

state_response.summary: Sources do not report a response to this protest; response remains unknown.

state_target.summary: The reports name the General Electricity Company of Libya (GECOL) in connection with salary arrears, but the opened passages do not establish its ownership or status as a domestic state actor.

notes: Alwasat and Libya Observer are different outlets but both may depend on the union statement. They name the General Electricity Company of Libya (GECOL) in connection with the arrears, but the opened passages do not establish the company’s ownership or status as a domestic state actor. Eligibility remains pending state-target review and the 50-person threshold; workforce scope and work stoppage are not attendance counts.
open_questions: Do the opened reports or another source establish GECOL as a domestic state actor and clarify the target of the demand?
Was 50 or more people simultaneously present at the protest?
What was the exact venue and when did it physically end?
Did the named company or responsible officials receive the demands or respond?

title: Tripoli teachers' sit-in for implementation of salary-increase law
scope: Single reported sit-in; broader linked protest series not yet established
participants_original: Teachers held a sit-in; no attendance estimate is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: No simultaneous participant estimate is reported in the opened account; the threshold is not established.

location.summary: The account places the sit-in outside the Presidential Council in Tripoli.

demands.summary: Teachers called for implementation of Law No.4 of 2018, which the report says would increase teacher salaries.

participants_original.summary: The article identifies teachers at a sit-in but reports no count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No participant estimate appears in the read passage.

start_date.summary: The article is published Jan27 and reports a sit-in but does not explicitly identify the physical action date; publication date is not treated as event date.

state_response.summary: The source reports demands but no official reception or event response.

notes: The report links the demand to the Tripoli Presidential Council and a teacher salary law. This is one reported act; do not infer a countrywide crowd or combine it with other salary actions. Exact occurrence date is unknown from the opened text.
open_questions: When did the sit-in physically occur and begin?
Did at least 50 teachers gather simultaneously?
Was an official meeting/reception held at the Council?

title: Libyan Tax Authority employees’ wage sit-in
location: Outside the Tax Authority, Tripoli (Jan31); exact location before Jan31 not stated
scope: Tripoli public sit-in documented Jan31; employee involvement across Tax Authority departments reported, but attendance or multi-city gatherings are not established
organizer: Tax Authority employees; no named union reported
participants_original: An unspecified number of Tax Authority employees; LANA reports a Jan31 sit-in outside the Tax Authority in Tripoli, and Sada says employees across departments were on the 22nd consecutive day. No headcount is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: No concurrent participant estimate is reported; the 18-day duration and workforce size do not establish 50 attendees.

start_date.summary: Al-Ain reported the sit-in's 18th consecutive day on Jan27; Sada reported its 22nd consecutive day on Jan31; LANA confirms the Jan31 sit-in continued. This supports a January start at month precision only; no exact day is claimed.

location.summary: LANA reports a public sit-in outside the Tax Authority in Tripoli on Jan31; no earlier venue is established.

scope.summary: LANA describes employees of the Tax Authority across Libya as claimants, but places the physical Jan31 sit-in outside the Tripoli authority; Sada reports an action across departments without establishing that all employees or branches attended simultaneously.

demands.summary: Al-Ain and Sada describe opposition to a 20% salary reduction and Sada mentions health insurance; LANA reports demands to the Ministry of Finance for salary adjustment/parity with Administrative Control Authority and Audit Bureau employees. The attributed descriptions are not reconciled.

participants_original.summary: All accounts identify employees at a sit-in, but none gives a concurrent attendance count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No source gives an attendance count or estimate of 50+; duration and employee population are not attendance.

state_response.summary: Sources report demands directed to state authorities and continuation, but do not report official reception or other event response; all seven response fields remain unknown.

notes: Jan27 Al-Ain and Jan31 Sada reports give 18th- and 22nd-day counters, which align with a January onset but do not explicitly date it. LANA confirms an actual Jan31 public sit-in outside the Tax Authority in Tripoli and attributes parity demands to a statement by employees. Reports differ in how they describe the salary dispute; retain their source attributions pending clarification. Employee totals/duration are not crowd counts.
open_questions: What was the exact start date, and did this same gathering continue beyond Jan31?
Did 50 or more employees gather at the Tripoli site simultaneously?
Were additional branch locations gathering concurrently, or was the action localized to Tripoli?
How do the attributed accounts of the 20% salary decision and salary-parity demand relate?
Did the Ministry of Finance or Presidential Council receive/respond to the demands?

title: Hariga Brigade personnel’s Jan5 protest stand over salary arrears
location: Hariga/Tobruk area; the Jan5 protest-stand caption gives no precise venue, while the associated oil-export blockade is reported at Hariga port
scope: Alwasat’s later photo caption labels a public protest stand (وقفة احتجاجية) by Hariga Brigade elements on Jan5. Contemporary Libya Observer reporting describes an armed export blockade over the same salary issue; same-day actor/issue context is preserved as one possible episode, not split automatically into a second unique event. The caption does not establish crowd size or exact venue.
organizer: Hariga Brigade / Petroleum Facilities Guard personnel; no union reported
participants_original: An unspecified number of Hariga Brigade / PFG personnel at the Jan5 protest stand. Libya Observer reports more than 1,000 brigade members were owed salaries; this is unit membership, not people gathered.
threshold_50_evidence: A report caption identifies a physical protest stand on Jan5, but no concurrent attendee estimate is provided. The reported 1,000 unpaid PFG members cannot be used as crowd size.

start_date.summary: Alwasat’s photo caption dates the protest stand (وقفة احتجاجية) to Jan5 2021; Libya Observer dates the associated Hariga port blockade to Jan5.

location.summary: The caption names Hariga Brigade but gives no precise protest-stand venue. Libya Observer locates the contemporaneous armed blockade at Hariga oil port in Tobruk; exact overlap between the protest stand and blockade site is uncertain.

organizer.summary: The caption identifies Hariga Brigade elements; Libya Observer names the Hariga Brigade of the Petroleum Facilities Guard.

demands.summary: Contemporaneous reports attribute the protest/blockade to delayed salary payments, reportedly unpaid for more than a year.

participants_original.summary: PFG personnel are identified; no attendance number is reported. The 1,000 figure refers to unpaid brigade personnel under command.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No concurrent crowd count or 50+ estimate. The image caption is not counted, and brigade strength is not attendance.

state_response.summary: The Jan7 report says municipal officials and city elders intervened and a port source described a two-week deadline to NOC; it does not document a direct official reception of demonstrators or actual salary payment. All seven response fields remain unknown.

notes: Retained as a provisional public protest-stand lead because Alwasat’s caption explicitly labels a Jan5 وقفة احتجاجية. The same-date, actor and salary context of Libya Observer’s armed export blockade leaves the episode boundary unresolved; do not split it into a second unique event automatically. The caption does not establish crowd size, precise venue or duration, and the armed blockade is not evidence of mass attendance.
open_questions: Was a public protest stand held separately from, or as part of, the Jan5 armed port blockade?
Did 50 or more people gather simultaneously at the protest stand?
Where exactly was the stand, and when did any physical assembly end?
Did a responsible public authority directly receive or fulfill the salary demands?
